local_name_source: Bakuradze et al., 2020; Saber Bakhtiari and Mahnaz Talebi-Dastenaei, field notes 2017
language_distribution_estimate: Phereydnuli Georgian 35%; Esfahān Persian group 30%; Tehrāni type Persian 25%; Esfahan Province Turkic 5%; Lori-Bakhtiāri of Esfahan Province 5%

notes: Ali Babaei (field notes 2022) notes that in 1956, this town comprised two villages of equivalent population: Miān Dasht (Toreli), with Georgian inhabitants, and Buin, which was mixed between Georgian and Judeo-Khunsāri speakers. In 1998, the Persian-speaking village of Shesh Javān (local name: Shishegun) was incoporated into the town.

notes: Ali Babaei (field notes, 2022) notes that, with the exception of some families from Khānsar, the population of this town is ethnically Georgian. Since around 1980, Georgian has no longer been passed on to children as a mother tongue.
